page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-480GB-2xB200 is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 48 vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8570 processors running at 2.0 GHz on an x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization. The system features 480.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.0 GB per core. The primary hardware highlight is the inclusion of two NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs, delivering a total of 384 GB of VRAM. Notably, this instance does not include local storage, meaning external storage solutions must be utilized.

Benchmark results indicate exceptional multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier ratings in PassMark CPU score, PassMark CPU physics, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth also registers in the top 10% tier at 385.14 GB/sec. For AI workloads, prompt processing for a small 135M LLM model reaches a top-tier speed of 9458.91 tokens/sec, while text generation operates at a strong 317.76 tokens/sec. Single-core performance is more moderate, placing in the middle 50% average tier.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers a high ratio of GPU memory and system RAM relative to the CPU core count, making it highly efficient for memory-intensive parallel processing. However, the CPU allocation is designated as shared, which may introduce performance variability under sustained, non-GPU-bound computational loads. The lack of local storage requires architectural planning for data-intensive pipelines, balancing the high-performance GPU capabilities against external storage latency.

This server is designed for workloads requiring massive parallel processing and substantial GPU memory. Suitable use cases include large language model inference, deep learning training, high-performance database operations, and complex physics simulations.
